translationRepairs: Shichang fought from the Zhiyuan, the fiercest ship in the fleet, matched against the Japanese Yoshino and Nisshin; the Yoshino was the backbone of the enemy line.
Shichang fought from the Zhiyuan, the fiercest ship in the fleet, matched against the Japanese Yoshino and Naniwa; the Yoshino was the backbone of the enemy line.
s0070 pairs 吉野 with 浪速. 浪速 is the Japanese cruiser Naniwa; Nisshin (日進) is a different ship and is not in the Chinese. The proposed replacement correctly names Naniwa.
Shichang was caught in an air pocket and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw him and ordered a boat to hurry to his rescue.
Shichang was kept afloat by a life buoy and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw him and ordered a boat to hurry to his rescue.
s0076 has 身環氣圈不沒, and s0077 縮臂出圈 shows he could slip an arm free of the 圈. 氣圈 is a life buoy/flotation ring, not an underwater air pocket; the proposed idiomatic English corrects that.
Shichang's body was ringed by an air pocket and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw this and ordered a rescue boat sent at speed.
Shichang's body was ringed by a life buoy and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw this and ordered a rescue boat sent at speed.
The same 氣圈 in s0076 is a life buoy encircling his body (身環…圈). Literal 'air pocket' is wrong; 'life buoy' matches the Chinese and the following 出圈.
He refused to be pulled aboard, slipped his arm from the air pocket, and drowned.
He refused to be pulled aboard, slipped his arm from the life buoy, and drowned.
s0077 縮臂出圈 continues the flotation-ring sense of 氣圈 from s0076. 'Air pocket' is wrong; 'life buoy' is the accurate idiomatic reading.

The Jiyuan fled with Japanese ships in pursuit; Commander Fang Boyian ran up a white flag, which only made the pursuit fiercer; a sailor fired back and knocked down the enemy's signal mast; Boyian then falsely claimed a victory and withdrew to block the eastern and western entrances to Weihai.

The Jiyuan fled with Japanese ships in pursuit; Commander Fang Boqian ran up a white flag, which only made the pursuit fiercer; a sailor fired back and knocked down the enemy's signal mast; Boqian then falsely claimed a victory and withdrew to block the eastern and western entrances to Weihai.

s0062 names 方柏謙 / 柏謙. Standard pinyin is Fang Boqian / Boqian; idiomatic 'Boyian' is a corrupted romanization, and the proposed forms restore the correct reading without changing the rest of the sentence.

When the Japanese came up, he directed the gun crews in their defense; after three hours of fierce fighting three enemy ships were sunk, and he covered the landing of eight battalions of Liu Mingchuan's army by holding the sea long enough for them to get ashore.

When the Japanese came up, he directed the gun crews in their defense; after three hours of fierce fighting three enemy ships were sunk, and eight battalions of the Ming Army were transported and able to land by seizing the interval.

s0097 has 運送銘軍八營，得以乘間登岸. 銘軍 is the Ming Army; the Chinese does not name Liu Mingchuan, and 運送 is transport, not covering a landing by holding the sea. The proposed English removes the invented personal name and restores the source sense.
Shichang then drove the screws at full speed in a fury, intending to ram the Yoshino and perish together; he was struck by its torpedo and the boiler ship split apart and sank.
Shichang then drove the screws at full speed in a fury, intending to ram the Yoshino and perish together; he was struck by its torpedo, the boilers burst, and the ship split apart and sank.
s0075 ends 中其魚雷，鍋船裂沉. 鍋 and 船 are separate: the boilers and the ship split/burst and sank. Fusing them as 'boiler ship' is wrong; the proposed literal separates boilers and ship correctly.
